subject: Coverage slab adjustment and departure path discussion
messages:
From: Alesia Novak <alesia.novak@heliotex.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@heliotex.com
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — Replacement economics and minimum coverage slab

Markus,

Thanks for the quick intro call this morning. We ran a quick finance check and there are two levers we need to understand before recommending Redwood internally: (1) how bridge/exit credits would be structured if we move from our incumbent for inference, and (2) an explicit coverage slab for committed throughput so our SRE and finance teams can reconcile pricing risk.

High level asks:
- A simple worked example showing credits if we commit to a 12-month ramp vs a 3-month pilot.
- What minimum committed slab (monthly token equivalent) gives us predictable unit pricing and where the step-changes are.
- Any SLA carveouts or onboarding accelerator credits you can offer for a go-live within 45 days.

We're under a procurement review next Wednesday and would like a short, actionable summary that we can attach. If you can send a one-pager and a simple spreadsheet, that'd be ideal.

Cheers,
Alesia Novak
Head of Platform Finance
Heliotex Systems

Attachment: none
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alesia Novak <alesia.novak@heliotex.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Initial ask — Replacement economics and minimum coverage slab

Alesia —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a short spreadsheet with two worked scenarios and a one-page summary:
- Scenario A: 3-month pilot (no commit) — we offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 20% of expected first 3 months' bill to offset migration effort.
- Scenario B: 12-month committed slab — we propose a tiered bridge credit (applied as bill credits over the first 6 months) scaled to the commit: 10% credit for the first $100k run-rate, 6% for the next $200k. That yields a larger upfront commercial swing without permanently lowering unit price.

Coverage slab guidance:
- Minimal predictable slab: ~75M tokens/month to hit our mid-tier unit pricing.
- Step changes: 75M, 250M, 1B tokens — each step unlocks more aggressive quantization/throughput bundling and lower per-token.

SLA/onboarding:
- We can commit to a 45-day onboarding target with an onboarding SLA credit (attached template). If go-live misses the date due to Redwood delays, we apply a monthly service credit up to 5% for the first two months.

Files attached: redwood-bridge-credit-sheet.xlsx, sla-exception-template.pdf

Next step: if this structure looks roughly aligned, Vanessa (cc'd) will propose a counter that balances upfront credits and a modest term commitment. Happy to jump on a 30-minute pricing call today.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Global Sales — Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Initial ask — Replacement economics and minimum coverage slab

Alesia —

Quick commercial note on the bridge credit math so procurement has a clean counter to review:
- If Heliotex commits to a 12-month slab at >=100M tokens/month we can firm up a 8% bridge credit applied monthly for the first 6 months (reduced from Markus' initial 10%) in exchange for a 12-month minimum term and a 60-day prepay option to smooth cash.
- For a 3-month pilot we hold the onboarding credit at 20% but can add a one-time professional services credit of up to $15k toward workload porting (to accelerate the 45-day timeline).

Operational caveat: to provide the 8% bridge on a 12-month commit we need a signed SLA exception (we'll use the attached template) that limits rollback credits if usage drops below 60% of the slab in months 7–12. This preserves economics while giving you a predictable glide path.

Request: please confirm which path Procurement prefers (pilot vs 12-month slab) and whether legal can accept the SLA carve. If they prefer, we can mark up the DocuSign and request a procurement review copy by EOD Friday.

Thanks — V.
